content.comment_body: Thanks in advance for your help. I am working on a wye/delta motor starter and struggling a bit with function block programming. I tried ladder diagram programming in [product_name] [version_no], but when I add a timer to the ladder, there is no output available on the timer block. My goal is to energize input I1 and have outputs Q1 and Q2 energized. After 2 seconds, I want Q3 to be energized and Q2 to be de-energized. However, I can't find a timer output to connect to Q3. Any advice would be appreciated.

In [product_name]'s ladder diagram editor, timer blocks do not have direct digital outputs. To check a timer's status, you need to use a make contact. Select the timer you want in the block properties of the make contact. Please see the attachment.
Thank you for your assistance. Your help is greatly appreciated.
Hello, if ladder programming is unfamiliar, why not use function block diagram instead? For beginners, function block diagram tends to be easier.

analysis.insight_summary: Users experience confusion with the timer block in ladder diagram mode within [product_name] [version_no], mainly due to the lack of a direct output for sequential control. The requirement to use a separate make contact block to access the timer state is not clearly documented in the software interface or help files, which leads to difficulties implementing timer-driven logic.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect timer blocks in ladder logic to offer a straightforward output for driving sequential events. They look for an intuitive way to set up timed output transitions using [product_name].
